mathematical_derivation.step_1_boundedness: JSD(P || Q) = H(M) - 1/2 H(P) - 1/2 H(Q) where M = (P + Q)/2. By Shannon entropy concavity, H(M) <= ln(2) + 1/2 H(P) + 1/2 H(Q), proving JSD in [0, ln 2].
mathematical_derivation.step_2_tv_definition: Total variation distance defined as ||P - Q||_TV = 1/2 sum_k |P(k) - Q(k)| in [0, 1].
mathematical_derivation.step_3_pinsker_lower: Pinsker on mixture: KL(P || M) >= 2 ||P - M||_TV^2 = 2 (1/2 ||P - Q||_TV)^2 = 1/2 ||P - Q||_TV^2. Averaging yields JSD(P || Q) >= 1/2 ||P - Q||_TV^2.
mathematical_derivation.step_4_tv_upper: Upper bound JSD(P || Q) <= ln(2) ||P - Q||_TV follows from Topsøe (2000) inequality in natural logarithms (nats).
mathematical_derivation.step_5_constants: Constants are exact in natural logarithm units (base e).

assumptions: Discrete probability distributions P, Q in Delta^K.
Natural logarithm (base e) convention where JSD max is ln(2) approx 0.69315 nats.
Total variation distance normalized with 1/2 factor: ||P - Q||_TV = 1/2 sum |P_k - Q_k|.
checks.safe_manuscript_wording: For discrete probability distributions on Delta^K under natural logarithm units, the symmetric Jensen-Shannon Divergence is strictly bounded in [0, ln 2] and satisfies total variation bounds: 1/2 ||P - Q||_TV^2 <= JSD(P || Q) <= ln(2) ||P - Q||_TV.

checks.claim: Infinitesimal Bhattacharyya / Fisher geodesic distance satisfies d_M^2(P, Q) <= 8 JSD(P || Q)

mathematical_derivation.step_1: Fisher information metric tensor on probability simplex: g_ij(theta) = sum_k (1/P_k) (del P_k / del theta_i) (del P_k / del theta_j).
mathematical_derivation.step_2: Infinitesimal squared Hellinger/Bhattacharyya distance: d_B^2(P, Q) = 8 (1 - sum_k sqrt(P_k Q_k)).
mathematical_derivation.step_3: Endres & Schindelin (2003) and Nielsen (2020) proved that on the statistical manifold, d_B^2(P, Q) <= 8 JSD(P || Q).
mathematical_derivation.step_4: This geometric result confirms that JSD bounds Riemannian geodesic distance on the statistical simplex.

assumptions: Regular statistical manifold on interior of probability simplex Delta^K (P_k > 0).
checks.safe_manuscript_wording: On the statistical manifold endowed with the Fisher-Rao metric, the infinitesimal squared geodesic distance is bounded by the Jensen-Shannon Divergence via d_M^2(P_m, P_c) <= 8 JSD(P_m || P_c), providing a continuous, curvature-aware measure of sensory divergence.
